# F-Droid metadata

App listings for the [F-Droid](https://f-droid.org) repository that publishes
this project's two Android apps, so they can be installed and updated from a
phone instead of being sideloaded with `adb install`.

```
metadata/com.lunchbox_os.companion.yml
metadata/com.lunchbox_os.media.yml
```

## Who reads these files

**Not this repository's CI.** The repository is generated by a service running
inside the [`fahrengit-451`](https://github.com/aarmea/fahrengit-451) stack that
hosts the F-Droid repository. After each release it downloads the release's
`.apk` assets, fetches *this directory at the release tag*, and runs
`fdroid update`. Nothing here is pushed anywhere; it is pulled.

That means a mistake in these files surfaces on the server, minutes after a tag,
where nobody is watching — which is why `release.yml` runs
`lunchbox package fdroid` as a validation step on every release (and why you can
run the same command locally, below).

See [`docs/ai/history/2026-07-26 002 fdroid-repository.md`](../../docs/ai/history/2026-07-26%20002%20fdroid-repository.md)
for the design and [`003 fdroid-fahrengit-451-spec.md`](../../docs/ai/history/2026-07-26%20003%20fdroid-fahrengit-451-spec.md)
for the server side.

## Conventions

- **No version fields.** `fdroid update` reads `versionCode` and `versionName`
  out of the APK, so the repo-root `VERSION` stays the single source of truth and
  there is nothing here for `lunchbox version check` to police.
- **`AllowedAPKSigningKeys` pins the release certificate.** `fdroid update`
  refuses to publish an APK signed by any other key. Since the server republishes
  release assets with no human in the loop, this is the control that stops a
  wrongly-signed APK from reaching a family device as an in-place upgrade. It
  must be updated if the release signing key ever changes:

  ```sh
  apksigner verify --print-certs lunchbox-companion_X.Y.Z.apk | grep 'SHA-256 digest'
  ```

- **One file per `applicationId`**, named exactly after it.

## Testing changes locally

```sh
sudo apt install --no-install-recommends fdroidserver default-jdk-headless
./scripts/lunchbox package fdroid --debug-keys   # after building APKs
```

`--no-install-recommends` matters: it takes the dependency tree from ~269
packages / ~300 MB to ~67 / ~78 MB (matplotlib and tk arrive as Recommends of
androguard and are not needed). `default-jdk-headless` matters because
fdroidserver signs the index with `/usr/lib/jvm/default-java/bin/jarsigner` and
prefers that path over every other JDK on the machine — if the default is a JRE,
the run fails at the very end with an opaque `OSError`.

`--debug-keys` drops the signing-key pin, which debug-signed local builds would
otherwise fail. Omit it when validating real release APKs. The generated repo
lands in `dist/fdroid-repo/` and can be served with any static file server to try
it on a phone:

```sh
python3 -m http.server -d dist/fdroid-repo 8080
# then add http://<host>:8080/repo in the F-Droid client
```
